Egress · Group I-4: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Which group the building is in decides every limit below; the architect states it, a person confirms.

Egress · Child day care classified Group E: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): More than five but not more than 100 children 2 1/2 or younger, in rooms on a level of exit discharge each with an exit door directly outside: Group E, not I-4; the architect states it.
Egress · Care during religious functions: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Part of the primary occupancy: the architect states it.
Egress · Five or fewer persons receiving care: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Part of the primary occupancy, not I-4: the architect states it.
Egress · Five or fewer persons in a dwelling unit: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Group R-3 or the Residential Code of New York State: the architect states it.

Egress · Covered and open mall buildings: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The building may hold a covered or open mall: whether it is a covered or open mall building of not more than three floor levels and three stories above grade plane, and so held to Section 402 (its foyers and lobbies of Groups B, R-1 and R-2 aside, exception 1), is a person's check.

Egress · A mall building's means of egress: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each tenant space and the mall are given means of egress by 402.8 and the code, 402.8.1 to 402.8.8 governing where they conflict: a person's check.

Egress · A mall taken as a corridor: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A mall may be taken as a corridor for egress, and need not meet 1005.1's capacity where it is as wide as 402.8.1.1 asks: a person's check.

Egress · A mall at least 20 ft wide: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The mall's aggregate clear egress width (at least 20 ft, enough for the occupants it serves) and the 10 ft clear to a height of 8 ft between a tenant space's projection and the nearest kiosk, bench, display or other obstruction are a person's check: kiosks and such aren't drawn.

Egress · A tenant space's occupant load: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each tenant space's occupant load is worked out as the code asks (Table 1004.5 by its function) and its means of egress sized on it: a person checks which rooms are tenant spaces.

Egress · The mall's occupant load by Equation 4-1: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The occupants the mall's means of egress serve come from the gross leasable area (anchor buildings left out) and Equation 4-1's occupant load factor, OLF = 0.00007 x GLA + 25 sq ft a person: a person works it out (tenant spaces with their own independent means of egress left out).

Egress · The mall's load factor: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Equation 4-1's factor need not be under 30 and may not exceed 50 sq ft a person: part of the person's check of the mall's occupant load (402.8.2.1).

Egress · Anchor buildings' occupants not counted in the mall's: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Anchor buildings opening into the mall are left out of the mall's occupants: part of the person's check of the mall's occupant load.

Egress · A food court's occupants added to the mall's: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A food court's occupant load (Section 1004) is added to the mall's from Equation 4-1 for the mall's means of egress: a person's check.

Egress · A tenant space's second means of egress: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A tenant space needs two means of egress where the travel to the mall from a point the public uses is over 75 ft or it holds 50 or more: the model doesn't say which rooms are tenant spaces or the mall, so a person checks.

Egress · An assembly occupancy of 500 or more in a covered mall building: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An assembly occupancy of 500 or more in a covered mall building has its entrance next to a principal entrance to the mall and at least half its required means of egress opening directly outside; in an open mall building its main exit may open to the open mall: a person's check.

Egress · Anchor buildings' means of egress independent of the mall's: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): An anchor building's required means of egress is independent of the mall's, the mall's egress never passes through an anchor building, and a mall ending at an anchor building with no other way out is a dead-end mall: a person's check.

Egress · Travel at most 200 ft in a tenant space and in the mall: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): In a tenant space, at most 200 ft from any point to an exit or the mall's entrance; in a covered mall, at most 200 ft from any point to an exit; in an open mall, at most 200 ft to an exit or the perimeter line: a person's check, the model not saying which rooms are tenant spaces or the mall.

Egress · Access to exits from a mall: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where more than one exit is required, travel in either direction from any point in a mall to separate exits (in an open mall, to two places on the perimeter line, neither an anchor building's or a parking garage's wall), an exit passageway or corridor from the mall at least 66 in wide, and a dead-end mall at most twice its narrowest width: a person's check.

Egress · Exit passageways from a tenant space built per Section 1024: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Exit passageways that give a tenant space its secondary means of egress are built per Section 1024: a person's check.

Egress · Service areas opening into exit passageways: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Mechanical and electrical rooms, service areas and service elevators may open directly into an exit passageway only where it is separated from them by 1-hour fire barriers (707) or horizontal assemblies (711), their openings rated 1 hour: a person's check.

Egress · Security grilles and doors in a required means of egress: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Sliding or rolling security grilles or doors in a required means of egress stay fully open while the public is in, are not closed with 10 or more people in spaces served by one exit or 50 or more served by more than one, open from within without special knowledge or effort, and take at most half the exits where two or more are required: a person's check.

Egress · High-rise buildings: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The building may be a high-rise: Sections 403.2 to 403.6 apply unless it is one of the exceptions (an airport traffic control tower, an open parking garage, a Group A-5 portion, a special industrial occupancy, or a building holding Group H-1, or Group H-2 or H-3 per the sections named): a person's check.

Egress · A story with three or more exits: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A story's count of exits is the rule “Exits per story by occupant load, one where 1006.3.4 allows (BCNYS 1006.3.3)”'s (Table 1006.3.3) and the distance between its farthest pair the rule “Two exits at least 1/2 the diagonal apart, 1/3 sprinklered (BCNYS 1007.1.1)”'s; whether the others are a reasonable distance apart is a person's judgment. Each space's own are the rule “A space needing three exits: two arranged per 1007.1.1 (BCNYS 1007.1.2)”.

Egress · Exit access stairways keep their separation: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Whether two exit access stairways or ramps keep the separation for all their length is not measured from the drawing yet: a person checks.
Egress · Three or more exit access stairways: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Not measured from the drawing yet: a person checks.

Egress · Intervening spaces in a building of two or more groups: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building of two or more groups: item 3 (Group H's hazard) and which room is which occupancy aren't marked; a person checks.

Egress · Multiple tenants: no egress through another tenant: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Which spaces are separate tenants is the architect's statement; a person checks the paths and the exception.

Egress · Table 1017.2 in a building of two or more groups: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building of two or more groups (two or more groups stated): 1004.4 applies the means of egress requirements to each portion by its own occupancy, and a component two occupancies share meets the more stringent; which room is which occupancy isn't marked yet, so a person checks.

Egress · Table 1017.2 note a: sections that change the distance: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A person checks whether the building has a mall, a Group I-2 or I-3 occupancy, a special amusement area, an aircraft manufacturing facility, a refrigeration machinery room or a refrigerated room, assembly seating, a temporary structure or a pedestrian walkway: each has its own distance (note a), a person's check.

Egress · Group H's sprinkler system: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Group H: the sprinklered columns ask for a system per 903.2.5 and 903.2.5.1 (Group H's own requirement, not brought in); the rows read the stated NFPA 13 system as one, a person confirms it.

Egress · Exterior egress balcony increase: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The design takes the increase: the balcony (Section 1021, not brought in) and its length are a person's check.
Egress · Groups F-1 and S-1 increase to 400 ft: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The increase's group: its conditions (not measured) are a person's check.
Egress · Group H-5 increase to 300 ft: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The increase's group: its conditions (not measured) are a person's check.

Egress · Travel within an atrium at most 200 ft: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Which part of a path is within an atrium, above or below the level of exit discharge, is not measured from the drawing yet: a person checks.

Egress · Group M merchandise pads: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Merchandise pads: their aisle accessways (30 in clear) and the 30 ft common path from any point in a pad (75 ft for not more than 50 occupants) are a person's check.

Egress · Fixed seating's common path: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Fixed seating in any group (an E school's auditorium, a B lecture hall): the common path from any seat (30 ft; 75 ft under 50 occupants; 50 ft smoke-protected or open-air) is a person's check.

Egress · Dead ends in a building of two or more groups: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building of two or more groups (two or more groups stated): 1004.4 applies the means of egress requirements to each portion by its own occupancy, and a component two occupancies share meets the more stringent; which room is which occupancy isn't marked yet, so a person checks.

Egress · Corridor rating in a building of two or more groups: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building of two or more groups: 1004.4 applies the means of egress requirements to each portion by its own occupancy, and a corridor two occupancies share meets the more stringent; which room is which occupancy isn't marked yet, so a person checks.
Egress · Group I-2 corridors: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Note a sends Group I-2 corridors to 407.2 and 407.3 (flags of Chapter 4 part c): a person checks.
Egress · Elevator hoistway doors protected: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Elevator hoistway doors in rated enclosures: Sections 716 and 3006.2 (not brought in), a person's check.

Egress · Corridor width in a building of two or more groups: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A building of two or more groups: 1004.4 applies the means of egress requirements to each portion by its own occupancy, and a corridor two occupancies share meets the more stringent (Group E's 72 in, Group I-2's 96 in); which room is which occupancy isn't marked yet, so a person checks.

Egress · Corridor width kept clear: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The corridor's width is measured between its walls and what the model draws in it; a door swinging into it, furniture or equipment the model doesn't show, and 1005.7's encroachments (its own flags since section group 5c) are a person's check.

Egress · Corridors not used as air ducts: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The air system isn't in the model: whether a corridor serves as a supply, return, exhaust, relief or ventilation duct, or a ceiling plenum above it is used as 1020.6.1 permits, is a person's check.

Egress · Stairway capacity: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The stairways' clear widths aren't measured: 0.3 in for each occupant of the story they serve (0.2 with a sprinkler system and a voice/alarm system, other than Groups H and I-2; assembly seating's own factors) is a person's check.

Egress · Other components' capacity: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Doors, ramps and exit passageways aren't measured for capacity: 0.2 in for each occupant they serve (0.15 with a sprinkler system and a voice/alarm system, other than Groups H and I-2) is a person's check. Corridors are the rule of their own.

Egress · Egress width never reduced toward the public way: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): The width or capacity required from a story never narrows along the path of egress travel to the public way: the routes measure each story's spaces and corridors, not the exits and discharge beyond them, so a person's check.

Egress · Losing one exit leaves half the capacity: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where more than one exit is required, losing any one exit (or access to it) leaves at least half the required capacity or width: the exits' widths aren't measured, so a person's check.

Egress · Converging stairways' capacity added: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Where egress from the stories above and below meets at an intermediate level, the capacity from there on is the larger of the widest minimum or the two stories' stairways' or ramps' required capacities added: the stairways aren't measured, so a person's check.

Egress · Doors take at most 7 in: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): A door fully open takes at most 7 inches of the required width, in any position at most half (latch hardware 34 to 48 inches up aside; not inside an R-2 dwelling or sleeping unit or an R-3 dwelling unit): the doors' swing into a corridor isn't drawn, so a person's check.

Egress · Trim at most 1 1/2 in each side into the width: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Handrails project as 1014.9 allows, trim and similar at most 1 1/2 inches each side (Group I-2 Condition 1 corridors per 407.4.3): projections aren't drawn, so a person's check.
Egress · Protruding objects per 1003.3: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Protruding objects meet 1003.3 (not brought in): a person's check.

Egress · Doors recognizable as doors: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Doors in the means of egress are easily recognizable as doors, carry no mirrors or similar reflecting materials and aren't concealed by curtains, drapes or decorations; exterior exit doors also meet 1022.2, gates 1010.4 and 1010.4.1, and turnstiles 1010.5 to 1010.5.4 (none brought in): what a door looks like isn't in the model, so a person's check. 1010.1.1's, 1010.1.2's and 1010.1.2.1's are rules of their own; 1010.1.3 to 1010.3.4 follow in section group 6c.

Egress · Each door's capacity for its occupant load: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): Each door opening's capacity is enough for the occupants it serves (1005.3.2: 0.2 in each, 0.15 in with a sprinkler system and an emergency voice/alarm system, other than Groups H and I-2): which occupants each door serves isn't worked out, so a person's check.

Egress · Nothing projects into a door's clear opening: A person checks this (Gordium doesn't decide it): No projection into a door's required clear width below 34 in, at most 4 in between 34 and 80 in, and door closers, overhead doorstops, frame stops, power operators and electromagnetic locks no lower than 78 in: door hardware isn't in the model, so a person's check.

definitions.text: HEIGHT OF BUILDING — he vertical distance measured from grade plane to the highest level of a flat or mansard roof or to the average height of a pitched, gabled, hip or gambrel roof, excluding bulkheads, housing for mechanical equipment, towers and similar constructions not intended for human occupancy or necessary equipment carried above roof level. Where a building contains sections of a roof of varying heights, the height of that building shall be measured using that section of the roof that has the highest elevation from grade plane.

GRADE PLANE — A reference plane representing the average of finished ground level on each side of the building at exterior walls. On the sides of the building where grade is level, the measurement will be taken at a point adjoining the building. Where the finished ground level slopes away from the exterior walls, the measurement shall be taken at the lowest point within the area between the building and the lot line or, where the lot line is more than six feet from the building, between the building and a point six feet from the building.

quotes.text: 1006.2.1 Egress based on occupant load and common path of egress travel distance. Two exits or exit access doorways from any space shall be provided where the design occupant load or the common path of egress travel distance exceeds the values listed in Table 1006.2.1. The cumulative occupant load from adjacent rooms, areas or spaces shall be determined in accordance
quotes.where: 1006.2.1, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: with Section 1004.2. Exceptions: 1. The number of exits from foyers, lobbies, vestibules or similar spaces need not be based on cumulative occupant loads for areas discharging through such spaces, but the capacity of the exits from such spaces shall be based on applicable cumulative occupant loads. 2. Care suites in Group I-2 occupancies complying with Section 407.4. 3. Unoccupied mechanical rooms and penthouses are not required to comply with the common path of egress travel distance measurement.

quotes.text: a.Buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. See Section 903 for occupancies where automatic sprin-

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1018.4 Aisle accessways in Group M. An aisle accessway shall be provided on not less than one side of each element within the merchandise pad. The minimum clear width for an aisle accessway not required to be accessible shall be 30 inches (762 mm). The required clear width of the aisle accessway shall be measured perpendicular to the elements and merchandise within the merchan- dise pad. The 30-inch (762 mm) minimum clear width shall be maintained to provide a path to an adjacent aisle or aisle accessway. The common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any point in the merchandise pad. Exception: For areas serving not more than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1018.4 Aisle accessways in Group M. An aisle accessway shall be provided on not less than one side of each element within the merchandise pad. The minimum clear width for an aisle accessway not required to be accessible shall be 30 inches (762 mm). The required clear width of the aisle accessway shall be measured perpendicular to the elements and merchandise within the merchan- dise pad. The 30-inch (762 mm) minimum clear width shall be maintained to provide a path to an adjacent aisle or aisle accessway. The common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any point in the merchandise pad. Exception: For areas serving not more than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm).
quotes.where: 1018.4, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.342
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1018.4 Aisle accessways in Group M. An aisle accessway shall be provided on not less than one side of each element within the merchandise pad. The minimum clear width for an aisle accessway not required to be accessible shall be 30 inches (762 mm). The required clear width of the aisle accessway shall be measured perpendicular to the elements and merchandise within the merchan- dise pad. The 30-inch (762 mm) minimum clear width shall be maintained to provide a path to an adjacent aisle or aisle accessway. The common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any point in the merchandise pad. Exception: For areas serving not more than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.

quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
quotes.where: 1030.8, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.355
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).

quotes.text: 1006.2.2 Egress based on use. The numbers, configuration and types of components of exits or access to exits shall be provided in the uses described in Sections 1006.2.2.1 through 1006.2.2.6. 1006.2.2.1 Boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms. Two exit access doorways are required in boiler, incinerator and furnace rooms where the area is over 500 square feet (46 m[fn2]) and any fuel-fired equipment exceeds 400,000 British thermal units (Btu) (422 000 KJ) input capacity. Where two exit access doorways are required, one is permitted to be a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the room. 1006.2.2.2 Refrigeration machinery rooms. Machinery rooms larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]) shall have not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Where two exit access doorways are required, one such doorway is permitted to be served by
quotes.where: 1006.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.315
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: a fixed ladder or an alternating tread device. Exit access doorways shall be separated by a horizontal distance equal to one-half the maximum horizontal dimension of the room. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigeration machinery room shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigeration machinery rooms or adjoining refriger- ated rooms or spaces. Exit and exit access doorways shall swing in the direction of egress travel and shall be equipped with panic hardware, regardless of the occupant load served. Exit and exit access doorways shall be tight fitting and self-closing. 1006.2.2.3 Refrigerated rooms or spaces. Rooms or spaces having a floor area larger than 1,000 square feet (93 m[fn2]), contain- ing a refrigerant evaporator and maintained at a temperature below 68°F (20°C), shall have access to not less than two exits or exit access doorways. Exit access travel distance shall be determined as specified in Section 1017.1, but all portions of a refrigerated room or space shall be within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of an exit or exit access doorway where such rooms are not protected by an approved auto- matic sprinkler system. Egress is allowed through adjoining refrigerated rooms or spaces. Exception: Where using refrigerants in quantities limited to the amounts based on the volume set forth in the Mechanical Code of New York State. 1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms. The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts. Panic hardware shall be provided where required in accordance with Section 1010.2.8.2. 1006.2.2.5 Vehicular ramps. Vehicular ramps shall not be considered as an exit access ramp unless pedestrian facilities are provided.
quotes.where: 1006.2.2.2, 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS), PDF p.316
quotes.document: 2025 Building Code of New York State (BCNYS)

quotes.text: 1030.8 Common path of egress travel. The common path of egress travel for a room or space used for assembly purposes having fixed seating shall not exceed 30 feet (9144 mm) from any seat to a point where an occupant has a choice of two paths of egress travel to two exits. Exceptions: 1. For areas serving less than 50 occupants, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 75 feet (22 860 mm). 2. For smoke-protected or open-air assembly seating, the common path of egress travel shall not exceed 50 feet (15 240 mm).
